source.author: Written for this study guide

questions.stem: A field extraction is saved with the Field Extractor. Which events does it apply to?

options.text: Every already-indexed event of that source type or source, and all future ones, with no reindex needed.
options.explanation: The Field Extractor creates a search-time extraction. It runs when a search runs, so it applies retroactively and needs neither a reindex nor a restart.

options.text: Only events indexed from that point forward.
options.explanation: That would be index-time behaviour. Search-time extractions are evaluated against data already on disk.

options.text: Every already-indexed event, but only after the index is rebuilt.
options.explanation: No reindex is involved. Nothing is rewritten on disk.

options.text: Only events returned by the search that was open when the extraction was created.
options.explanation: The extraction is a knowledge object scoped to a source type or source, not to one search.

questions.overallExplanation: Everything the Field Extractor builds is search-time. This is the single most useful fact in section 4.0, because it rules out any answer mentioning reindexing, restarts, or forward-only application.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform regex field extractions using the Field Extractor (FX)
guide.verdictNote: Contrast with rex, which is a search command rather than a knowledge object: its fields last for one pipeline and appear nowhere in Settings.

docs.title: Build field extractions with the field extractor (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: The field extractor generates search-time field extractions.

questions.stem: At the Save step of the Field Extractor, what is the default permission, and what does it mean?

options.text: Owner, meaning the extraction only runs in searches by the person who created it.
options.explanation: Owner is the default of the three choices, and the documentation states it only extracts fields in searches run by the creator.

options.text: App, meaning everyone using the current app sees the fields.
options.explanation: App is one of the three choices but it is not the default. Sharing is a deliberate step.

options.text: All apps, meaning the extraction is global immediately.
options.explanation: This is the widest of the three options and is furthest from the default.

options.text: There is no permission choice at the Save step; permissions are set later under Settings.
options.explanation: The choice is offered at Save. It can also be changed later, but it is present in the wizard.

questions.overallExplanation: The three choices are Owner, App and All apps, and the default is Owner. A colleague reporting that they cannot see your new field is almost always this default rather than a broken extraction.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform regex field extractions using the Field Extractor (FX)
guide.verdictNote: The same private-by-default rule governs field aliases and calculated fields, so it is worth learning once and applying across sections 4.0 and 5.0.

docs.title: Field extractor: Save step (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Permissions default to Owner; the choices are Owner, App, All apps.

questions.stem: Which Field Extractor step exists only on the regular expression path and not on the delimiter path?

options.text: Validate
options.explanation: The regex path runs Select Sample, Select Method, Select Fields, Validate, Save. The delimiter path has no Validate step.

options.text: Select Method
options.explanation: Both paths pass through Select Method; that is where the two paths diverge.

options.text: Save
options.explanation: Both paths end at Save.

options.text: Select Sample
options.explanation: Both paths start at Select Sample, unless the wizard was opened from Event Actions on a specific event.

questions.overallExplanation: Regex path: Select Sample, Select Method, Select Fields, Validate, Save. Delimiter path: Select Sample, Select Method, Rename Fields, Save. Anything that lives on the Validate step, such as counterexamples, exists only for regex extractions.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform delimiter field extractions using the FX
guide.verdictNote: Opening the extractor from Event Actions, Extract Fields on a specific event starts at Select Method, because the source type and sample are already decided.

docs.title: Field extractor: Select Method step (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: The two method paths and the steps each one visits.

questions.stem: When should the Delimiters method be chosen over the Regular Expression method?

options.text: When values are cleanly separated by a common character and are consistent across events, as in CSV-style data.
options.explanation: The documentation describes the delimiters method as designed for structured, table-based data where all fields are separated by a common delimiter.

options.text: When the data is unstructured and the field positions vary between events.
options.explanation: Varying structure is precisely the case for a regular expression. Delimiters need consistency.

options.text: When the events contain no repeating patterns at all.
options.explanation: Delimited data is highly repetitive by definition; that repetition is what makes the method work.

options.text: When the fields must be extracted at index time rather than search time.
options.explanation: Both methods produce search-time extractions. Neither touches index time.

questions.overallExplanation: Delimiters are for structured, table-based data. The reversed claim, that delimiters are for data without headers or for unstructured data, appears repeatedly in third-party study material and is wrong.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform delimiter field extractions using the FX
guide.verdictNote: The Udemy practice course states the reverse of this five separate times, which is recorded in the fact-check. Answer from the Select Method page.

docs.title: Field extractor: Select Method step (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: Delimiters suit structured data such as .csv files or events with a common separator.

questions.stem: Which field does the `rex` command read from when no `field=` argument is given?

options.text: `_raw`
options.explanation: field defaults to _raw on rex. erex has the same default under a different option name, fromfield.

options.text: `_time`
options.explanation: _time holds the event timestamp and is not a text field to run a pattern against.

options.text: The first field in the Selected Fields list
options.explanation: The sidebar's field selection is a display concern and has no bearing on command defaults.

options.text: There is no default; `field=` is required.
options.explanation: It is optional. The command with no field argument is valid and very common.

questions.overallExplanation: rex takes an optional field, defaulting to _raw. erex takes fromfield, also defaulting to _raw. extract has neither and can only read _raw, which is why extracting from a substring requires renaming that field to _raw first.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform regex field extractions using the Field Extractor (FX)
guide.verdictNote: The documented workaround for extract is `rename _raw AS temp uri_query AS _raw`, then extract, then rename back.

questions.stem: What is the default of `max_match` on `rex`, and what does `max_match=0` mean?

options.text: Default 1; 0 means unlimited matches.
options.explanation: Only the first match is kept by default. Setting 0 removes the cap, and any value above 1 produces a multivalue field.

options.text: Default 1; 0 means no matches are kept.
options.explanation: Zero means unlimited here, exactly as it does for limit on chart and top.

options.text: Default 0, meaning unlimited unless restricted.
options.explanation: The default is restrictive, not permissive. One match is kept unless you ask for more.

options.text: Default 10, matching the general series limit.
options.explanation: There is no ten-match default. Ten is the series limit on chart and timechart.

questions.overallExplanation: max_match defaults to 1, so a pattern that could match several times per event quietly keeps only the first. Raising it above 1 produces a multivalue field, and 0 means unlimited.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform regex field extractions using the Field Extractor (FX)
guide.verdictNote: A related subtlety: if a capture group can match repeatedly within itself, only the last capture is kept regardless of max_match.

questions.stem: What determines whether a field appears under Interesting Fields in the fields sidebar?

options.text: It appears in at least 20 percent of the events returned by the current search.
options.explanation: The threshold is measured against the events this search returned, so changing the search changes the list.

options.text: It appears in at least 20 percent of the events in the index.
options.explanation: The denominator is the current result set, not the index. This is the most common misreading.

options.text: It appears in at least 20 percent of the events of that source type.
options.explanation: Source type is not the denominator either. The measure is per search.

options.text: Splunk has classified it as important based on how often it is searched.
options.explanation: There is no usage-based ranking involved. It is a mechanical percentage.

questions.overallExplanation: Interesting Fields is a display rule for the sidebar only. A field present in 5 percent of events is fully extracted and fully searchable; it simply does not clear the bar for that list.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform regex field extractions using the Field Extractor (FX)
guide.verdictNote: On a fresh search, Selected Fields contains exactly host, source and sourcetype. index is a default field on every event, so it clears the bar and appears under Interesting Fields.

docs.title: Use fields to search (Search Tutorial 10.4)
docs.note: Interesting Fields lists fields appearing in at least 20 percent of the returned events.

questions.stem: Which two statements about case sensitivity in field extraction and search are true? (Choose two.)

options.text: Field names are case sensitive.
options.explanation: `sourcetype=x` and `SOURCETYPE=x` are different searches, and only the lowercase form matches the real field.

options.text: Field values are not case sensitive in the search command.
options.explanation: `status=Failed` matches an event whose stored value is failed.

options.text: Regular expressions in an extraction are case insensitive by default.
options.explanation: Splunk regular expressions are case sensitive unless the pattern says otherwise, for example with an inline (?i) flag.

options.text: Field names and values are both case insensitive at search time.
options.explanation: Names are case sensitive. Treating both the same way is the error the exam probes.

questions.overallExplanation: Names are case sensitive, values are not, and the exception is that eval and where expressions are case sensitive throughout. That three-part rule covers nearly every case-sensitivity question on this exam.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform regex field extractions using the Field Extractor (FX)
guide.verdictNote: Whether tag names are case sensitive is genuinely unsettled in the 10.4 documentation, which is why three questions in the transcribed practice bank are marked disputed and excluded from mock exams.

docs.title: search command (SPL Search Reference 10.4)
docs.note: Field names are case sensitive; field values are not.

questions.stem: A delimiter extraction discovers six fields. How many must be renamed before the wizard will let you save?

options.text: At least one; the rest keep names such as field1 and field2.
options.explanation: You must select and rename at least one field to reach Save. Unrenamed fields keep their auto-assigned names.

options.text: All six.
options.explanation: Renaming everything is good practice but is not enforced by the wizard.

options.text: None; renaming is entirely optional.
options.explanation: At least one rename is required to progress, so it is not fully optional.

options.text: Exactly half, so the extraction has a mix of named and generated fields.
options.explanation: There is no proportional rule of any kind.

questions.overallExplanation: One rename is the minimum to reach Save. Worth pairing with what each method writes: the regex method writes an inline EXTRACT- stanza into props.conf, while the delimiter method writes a transforms.conf stanza holding DELIMS and FIELDS.

guide.blueprintTitle: Perform delimiter field extractions using the FX
guide.verdictNote: The Rename Fields step offers four delimiter presets, Space, Comma, Tab and Pipe. Anything else, such as a colon or semicolon, has to be typed into the Other box.

docs.title: Field extractor: Rename Fields step (Knowledge Management 10.4)
docs.note: At least one field must be renamed; presets are Space, Comma, Tab, Pipe and Other.
